# Data and memory

Edva's data model provides explicit control over memory layout, allocation, and
initialization without a tracing garbage collector or runtime type overhead.

## Composite data structures

| Syntax and shape | Storage & Layout | Element / Field Count | Mutation Model | Index / Lookup Failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(x: Int, y: Int)`<br>**Named Record** | Flat aggregate on stack/arena | Static field count | Immutable; rebind with `'` | Compile error on unknown field |
| `(Int, String)`<br>**Positional Record** | Flat tuple aggregate | Static field count | Immutable; rebind with `'` | Compile error on bad index `.0` |
| `(i8 * 16)`<br>**Homogeneous Record** | Fixed inline array | Fixed compile-time count | Elements mutable | Must-init before access |
| `(T){}`<br>**Growable Array** | Resizable heap buffer | `?array` | Append with `+=`, index write | Yields `< T | Error >` |
| `(T)[]`<br>**Slice View** | Non-owning pointer + len | `?slice` | Read-only view | Bounds check returns `< T | Error >` |
| `Key ^ Value`<br>**Key-Value Map** | Open-addressing hash table | `?map` | Key write: `m ^ k = v` | Lookup yields `< Value | Error >` |
| `Builder`<br>**Builder** | Mutable buffer `{ len, ptr, cap }` | `?builder` | In-place append `+=` | Write past cap reallocates |
| `String`<br>**String** | Immutable fat pointer `{ len, ptr }` | `?string` | Immutable; freeze from Builder | Indexing returns `Rune` or byte |

---

## Definite field initialization tracking

Edva does **not** zero-fill uninitialized composite records. When declaring a composite
variable (`p: Point`), the compiler tracks which fields are definitely written along
every execution branch:

```dva
#type Point (x: Int, y: Int)

setup_point: <> => Point
setup_point = flag =>
   p: Point
   p.x = 10
   flag
      | p.y = 20
      | p.y = 30
   p // Allowed: both x and y are definitely initialized along all paths
```

### Compiler initialization safety rules

| Violation | Diagnostic | Rule Description |
|---|---|---|
| Read before write | `E3130` | Reading `p.y` before writing it is rejected at compile time. |
| Homogeneous must-init | `E3131` | Homogeneous records (`(T * N)`) require a whole-value initialization before any element read/write. |
| Partial escape | `E3132` | Passing a partially initialized composite to a function or returning it is rejected. |

---

## Strings vs Builders

Strings and Builders have **no member access** (`.len` and `.data` are invalid).
All inspection and manipulation is performed via symbolic prefix operators:

| Operation | String (`s`) | Builder (`b`) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Creation | `"hello"` / `+b` | `{64}` | Allocate buffer with capacity `64` |
| Measure length | `?s` | `?b` | Current byte count |
| Buffer address | `&s` | `&b` | `RawPtr` address for FFI / syscalls |
| Pure append | `s + "world"` | `b + "world"` | Returns a *new* value (O(N) copy) |
| In-place append | N/A | `b += "world"` | Mutates existing buffer in place |
| Freeze | N/A | `+b` | In-place transfer into immutable `String` (resets builder to `{0, 0, 0}`) |
| Set length | N/A | `?b = bytes_read` | Sets active length (asserts `0 <= n <= cap`, aborts E4008) |
| CRLF / byte sequence | N/A | `b = (13, 10)` | Appends byte record directly (0..255 checked) |

Freeze `+b` transfers the underlying buffer in-place into an immutable `String` and
resets the `Builder` descriptor to `{0, 0, 0}`, preventing post-freeze aliased mutation.

```dva
#use libc

// Efficient I/O with zero-copy Builder freeze:
read_socket_line: Int => String
read_socket_line = fd =>
   b = {1024}
   n = libc::recv(fd, &b, 1024, 0)
   n [< 1] "" |
      ?b = n   // Set length to exact received count
      +b       // Freeze buffer into String without heap copy
```

### Non-allocating string segment comparison

Comparing a `String` with a tuple of strings (`str == (p1, p2, ...)`) checks
equality against concatenated segments without allocating an intermediate string:

```dva
path = "api/v1/users"
is_users_api = path == ("api/", "v1/", "users")
```

## Key-Value Maps (`Key ^ Value`)

Maps are open-addressing keyed containers. A map type uses `Key ^ Value`, with
`String`, `Int`, or `Addr` keys and any storable value type:

| Operation | Syntax Form | Result Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Insert or rebind | `map ^ key = value` | Unit (`()`) | Infallible write (in-place) |
| Fallible lookup | `map ^ key` | `< Value | Error >` | Out-of-bounds yields poisonous `Error` |
| Key membership | `map ^? key` | Flag `<>` | Fast `<+>` (present) or `<->` (absent) |
| Delete entry | `map ^- key` | Flag `<>` | Leaves tombstone; returns `<+>` if key existed |
| Entry count | `?map` | `Int` | Active live entry count |
| Entry iteration | `map @ (k, v) =>` | Unit (`()`) | Iterates all live (non-deleted) entries |

```dva
#type ScoreMap String ^ Int

scores = ScoreMap()
scores ^ "Alice" = 95
scores ^ "Bob" = 88

// Fallible lookup with unwrap-or-abort
alice_score = (scores ^ "Alice")!!
print_int $ alice_score // prints 95

// Key presence test
has_bob = scores ^? "Bob"
has_bob | print("Bob is enrolled")
```

## Raw memory and volatile operations

For low-level systems programming, embedded targets, and driver development:

| Operator | Syntax | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Address extraction | `Addr(val)` | Raw pointer conversion to `Addr` |
| Volatile typed load | `@[addr T]` | Read value of type `T` from raw memory address |
| Volatile typed store | `@[addr T] = val` | Write value of type `T` to raw memory address |
| Compile-time size | `#size(Type)` | Size in bytes of any primitive or composite type |

```dva
// Writing a 32-bit register at hardware memory address:
UART0_BASE = 0x4000c000
@[UART0_BASE i32] = 0x01
```
